_note: Coordinates are in RAW capture pixels, same contract as the
efficiency-and-range figures. This capture is not a photograph of a screen:
it is drawn by the app's OWN renderer (CarPlayChipRenderer.renderDataFlow)
composited exactly as CarPlayChipTile composites it — rounded slate, raster
inset by contentPadding — so it is pixel-true to what the car draws and free
of capture artefacts. The canvas is 222x212 points at 3x device scale, hence
666x636 pixels; every point below is 3x the value the app's own geometry
functions report, which is how they were obtained rather than eyeballed.

images.name: internet-connection-tile
images.caption: Everything the tile is telling you. The bars carry no numbers and no fixed scale on purpose — taller is healthier, and the figure above them is the value. Watch the right-hand edge: bars climbing back out of the red, as they are here, mean coverage is returning.

callouts.label: What your phone claims it is on
callouts.detail: The radio your phone is attached to — 5G, LTE, or WI-FI.

callouts.label: How long a round trip took
callouts.detail: The app sends a tiny request and times the answer, in milliseconds. Lower is better; anything under a couple of hundred is a healthy link.

callouts.label: Tall and green: data flowing
callouts.detail: Each bar is one check, and the bars cover the last ten minutes. Height is health rather than speed, so a good link stands tall.

callouts.label: Amber: still working, but slowing
callouts.detail: The link is still carrying you, and answers are taking longer. This is usually what the edge of a cell looks like a minute before it goes.

callouts.label: Red stubs: nothing got through
callouts.detail: The checks went out and nothing came back. Your phone may still be showing full bars here — that is exactly the situation this tile exists to catch.
